endorsements.quote: The ideal team for this design work includes mental health clinicians, researchers, developers, individuals with lived eating disorder experience, and ethicists.

In our research, we have found that providing and demonstrating specific examples, especially at the earliest stages of AI tool codesign processes, elicits more certain feedback from participants (e.g., Beilharz et al. 2021 ; Sharp et al. 2025 ).

unlisted_practices: Provide crisis support contact details to AI chatbot users so they can connect with a human support service.

Design mental health chatbots to stop the conversation, urge immediate medical care, and alert the treating team when medical or psychiatric risk is detected, with user agreement to this risk assessment at the start of use.
Design AI tool tone to present factual information with an authentic validating tone, avoiding claims of feeling or empathy that sound inauthentic.
Use rule-based chatbots with preprogrammed answers where the highest level of safety is required.
Guide AI design and implementation using ethical frameworks for AI and digital technologies covering physical, cognitive, information, and governance domains.

screen.reason: This is an invited commentary discussing perceived barriers and ethical governance/codesign frameworks for deploying AI tools, particularly chatbots, in eating disorder care.
